GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
 Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru
 Updated - November 19, 2026 03:56 pm IST 
 Fabian Rodrigues READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 The official cover art for Grand Theft Auto VI, which launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on 19 November
 | Photo Credit: XBOX Wire & Rockstar Games
 This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.
 GTA VI: Gamers enter Vice City as most-awaited game is rolled out globally The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.
 GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮
 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes.
 We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow).
 We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November.
 Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨
— Albinder Dhindsa (@albinder) November 18, 2026 In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.
 For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.
 Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
 Your KRA is updated to completing missions and side quests 🎮 https://t.co/x1xSmUIPqU
— boAt (@RockWithboAt) November 18, 2026 Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.
 A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.
 Gamers watch a screen showing the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at a gaming centre in Buenos Aires on the day of the highly anticipated video game's release.
 | Photo Credit: 
 AFP
 One of the biggest differences between GTA VI and its predecessors for Indian players is how much of it was made here. Rockstar India’s Bengaluru studio reportedly has the largest team of any Rockstar office working on the game, with around 1,615 developers, and media reports credit it with building Vice Beach, a location on the map. Its roots go back to Dhruva Interactive, founded by Rajesh Rao in Bengaluru in 1997 and considered India’s oldest game developer when Rockstar folded it into Rockstar India in 2019. Rockstar India was established in 2016 and contributed to Red Dead Redemption 2 before turning to Leonida.
 The game follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals drawn into a conspiracy across Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, after a job goes wrong. Lucia is the series’ first female lead since it moved into three dimensions. The Vice City she drives through is a contemporary one, a far cry from the pastel-hued 1980s city many Indian players grew up with.
 Grand Theft Auto has always satirised America, and reviewers say the new game continues to do so with sharp digs at social media, celebrity culture and consumerism. The jokes should resonate in India, too. Livestreaming became a full-time career here largely on the back of mobile gaming, and Indian players will recognise the people of Leonida, many of whom seem to live for the camera.
 Reviews have been near-unanimously glowing. Within hours of reviews going live on November 18, the game scored 99 on Metacritic from nearly 150 critics, all positive. The site ranked it first of all time, ahead of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which scored 99 from 22 reviews in 1998. Critics have been particularly impressed by how alive Leonida feels and by its two leads, whose relationship evolves through the small choices players make along the way. Demand has been just as staggering, with Sensor Tower estimating nearly 16 million digital pre-orders worth over US$1.5 billion (around ₹14,000 crore) before the game unlocked at midnight on November 19. PlayStation and Xbox have both listed it as the most pre-ordered game in their stores’ history. Rockstar releases the game at midnight local time, which meant Indian players entered Leonida five and a half hours before London and 10 and a half hours before New York.
 GDAI launches India gaming report, highlights need for stronger funding The scale of the welcome says plenty about how much India has changed between instalments. When Grand Theft Auto V arrived in 2013, PUBG Mobile was still five years away, and many of the country’s biggest gaming channels had yet to upload their first videos. GTA VI lands in what Microsoft calls the world’s fastest-growing gaming market, with more than 500 million gamers. It is the first new Grand Theft Auto that India’s creator economy gets to welcome on launch day. Three of India’s biggest mobile-first channels, Total Gaming, Payal Gaming and Sharkshe, are even among the more than 30 creators on YouTube’s 24-hour global launch livestream.
 Now that the game is out, one of the Internet’s longest-running jokes has nowhere left to go, since nothing else can happen before GTA 6. The next ones will have to come from Leonida itself, and if Big Smoke is anything to go by, India will be quoting them for the next 20 years.
